records.statement: The Wilcoxon rank-sum test is presented as a nonparametric alternative for comparing two population central values with independent samples and is equivalent to the Mann-Whitney U test.
The Wilcoxon signed-rank test is presented as a nonparametric alternative for paired-data inference.

One-way analysis of variance compares population means across more than two groups under independence, equal-variance, and normality conditions; independence is the most critical of these design conditions.
Kruskal-Wallis is presented as a nonparametric alternative for comparing more than two population central values when the usual ANOVA conditions are unsuitable.
Hernán and Robins treat exchangeability, positivity, and consistency as core identifiability conditions for causal inference from observational data.
Randomization is valued because it is expected to produce exchangeability between treated and untreated groups with respect to potential outcomes.

Impact Evaluation in Practice distinguishes randomized assignment, instrumental variables, regression discontinuity, difference-in-differences, and matching as different strategies whose validity depends on their own assignment rules and assumptions.
The World Bank guidance explicitly identifies an equal-trends assumption as a key condition for difference-in-differences designs.
ICH E9 states that the precise definition of the primary variable used in analysis should be specified in the protocol to avoid multiplicity and post-hoc definition concerns.

ICH E9 treats prespecification, analysis sets, missing values/outliers, estimation and hypothesis testing, multiplicity adjustments, and subgroup/covariate analysis as distinct analysis-plan considerations.
Gamble et al. provide a minimum-content framework for statistical analysis plans intended to improve transparency and reproducibility of clinical-trial analysis.
